text:
casey: FYI CI is red on main, looks like a build failure in the pybind-based extension after yesterday's toolchain roll.

infra-bot: [buildkite] https://ci.example.com/builds/67321 - //third_party/pybind11:python_bindings failed on linux-gcc13

casey: paste of error (excerpt):
```
In file included from /usr/include/python3.10/pytime.h:9,
                 from /usr/include/python3.10/Python.h:100:
/opt/gcc-13/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/13/../../../../lib/libstdc++.so: undefined reference to `__stack_chk_guard'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

alex: :eyes: can someone try a local reproduce? guessing a linker/stdlib mismatch after the gcc image bump.

liu: I can repro in a container with the new image. sounds like we ended up linking against a different libgcc or missing -fPIC somewhere for a shared extension.

pat: quick note — pybind modules are sensitive to how we build third_party: we have some objects built without PIC in //third_party/fastmath and they get linked into the python shared object. toolchain change could make the system linker stricter.

sam: which CI shard is this? the linux sharedlib shard? I can force a rerun of that shard.

casey: linux-sharedlib-3, infra-bot linked above. sam can you rerun and add --artifact-collect? want full link line.

sam: rerun requested :white_check_mark: (job 67321.2 rerun)

infra-bot: rerun started, will post logs when done.

liu: while rerun is in flight, quick local repro steps I used:
```
docker run -it --rm redwood-ci/gcc:13 /bin/bash
git checkout main && bazel build //third_party/pybind11:python_bindings --spawn_strategy=local
# link line: bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/third_party/pybind11/_objs/python_bindings/python_bindings.so
```
The link line shows objects coming from //third_party/fastmath:fastmath_no_pic.a
```
/.../libfastmath.a(fastmath.o): relocation R_X86_64_32 against `.rodata' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
```

casey: that message nails it. fastmath got built without -fPIC and the new linker rejects it.

alex: any recent BUILD changes to third_party/fastmath? or did the toolchain roll change default pic flags? @pat

pat: no BUILD change. toolchain image bumped yesterday to gcc-13 which tightened default linker behaviour. we used to get away with non-PIC objects when linking static libs into a shared object; not anymore.

liu: short-term fix: rebuild fastmath with PIC. patch to add copts = ["-fPIC"] to //third_party/fastmath:BUILD and trigger a dedicated rebuild should green the shard.

sam: doing a targeted tryjob now with that copts change.

casey: can we also bisect the toolchain images to confirm regression? request if tryjob passes we revert the roll in the infra image registry and bisect later.

alex: agree. action items:
- sam: land a copts fix for fastmath and run tryjob (targeted)
- sam: if tryjob passes, open PR with revert-candidate for toolchain image and run full CI
- liu: run quick bisect between yesterday's toolchain images to see which gcc/libstdc++ change caused it
- casey: update incident thread if this will block any deploys

pat: noted — if we need a short-term workaround in bazel-toolchain we can also set a rule that enforces PIC for any target used by python shared objects.

sam: tryjob result: green on the shard (job 67321.try.1), link line now shows -fPIC objects.

casey: nice. please open the PR and mark it as hotfix. include the link to the tryjob in description.

sam: PR opened: https://git.example.com/r/redwood/infra/+/3456 - adds -fPIC to //third_party/fastmath and a changelog note. tagging @release for fast-track.

liu: bisect in progress, reproducer tested across images. preliminary: gcc-13.0.1 base image introduced stricter linker flags (ld 2.38) which enforces PIC for static objs linked into DSOs. will post exact commit.

alex: thanks everyone. once PR merges we'll watch canary and then roll forward with a coordinated toolchain bump that ensures PIC for third_party objects.

casey: leaving this thread open for the next 24h for monitoring. :thumbsup!
